LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.conditionalKlDiv: Given an input law r and channels W,V on measurable spaces, their conditional KL divergence is the extended nonnegative KL divergence between the joint laws obtained by sending the same input through W and V.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.conditionalKlDiv_: For any input law r, the conditional KL divergence of a channel W from itself is zero.

On finite discrete alphabets the conditional KL divergence of W from V under r is ∑ₓ r(x) D(W(·|x) ∥ V(·|x)) as an extended nonnegative number. A zero-weight row contributes zero, including when its divergence is infinite.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_conditiona: On finite discrete alphabets, suppose that at each x with r(x) > 0 every output allowed by W(·|x) is also allowed by V(·|x). The conditional KL divergence is finite and equals the real weighted sum ∑ₓ r(x)D(W(·|x) ∥ V(·|x)), omitting zero-weight rows.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.klDiv_channelJoin: For finite discrete alphabets, the extended KL divergence between joint laws p(x)W(y|x) and q(x)V(y|x) equals D(p∥q) plus the conditional KL divergence of W from V averaged with input law p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.toReal_klDiv_chan: If supp(p) ⊆ supp(q) and supp(W(·|x)) ⊆ supp(V(·|x)) for every x in supp(p), the KL chain rule on finite discrete alphabets is an equality of finite real numbers: the joint divergence is D(p∥q) plus the conditional divergence of W from V under p.
